name: H5N1 bird flu
value: 3 cattle-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Three Yakima County H5N1 cases in 2026, all linked to infected dairy cattle, one fatal; no human-to-human spread found
state: ECDC reported on 3 Nov that three Yakima County, Washington, residents have had H5N1 since mid-October, all with exposure to infected cattle; one died and two had mild illness (ECDC). UKHSA's report for the week to 1 Nov notes contact tracing and rates general public risk as low. Searches to 13 Nov found no newer human case, cluster or human-to-human spread, so these remain animal-to-human cases and the level stays Normal.
for_you: Public risk is rated low; it is higher for people in close contact with infected animals. UK readers can follow UKHSA and DEFRA guidance on avoiding contact with sick or dead birds and animals.
rubric_hit: Normal: sporadic animal-to-human cases only (three cattle-exposed cases in Washington, no human-to-human spread)

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
